reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational structure of learning behavior is modeled through a sequence of discrete reinforcement events contributing to habit formation. Each reinforcement adds a unit increment to habit strength, forming a series of diminishing contributions. As N increases, these increments become infinitesimal, indicating a limiting process. Cumulative habit strength H(N) aggregates these increments, producing a monotonically increasing but eventually flattening profile. This behavior aligns with negative acceleration dynamics, where the rate of change decreases over time. The resulting curve represents a fundamental learning function, serving as a kernel for deriving more complex theoretical constructs. The notched nature of the curve reflects the indivisibility of reinforcement units, ensuring discrete transitions rather than continuous flows. This discrete yet asymptotic model underpins both probabilistic inference in GSI and deterministic state evolution in GSE.
